scope: Static review of EE COP1 C.EQ.S/C.LT.S/C.LE.S, BC1F/T/FL/TL, CFC1 and CTC1 handling; no game execution, emulator, or hardware.

primary_manual.title: Sony EE Core Instruction Set Manual v6.0
primary_manual.host_note: The PDF is an SCE-authored manual served from a third-party mirror; the manual labels itself SCE Confidential.

software_comparator.title: PCSX2 FPU.cpp
software_comparator.scope: Independent software comparison, not silicon validation.

findings.compare_condition_bit: Matches for finite supported numeric operands and signed zero; C and unrelated FCR31 bits are set/cleared as expected from inspected templates.
findings.branch_condition_and_likely_delay: Inspected source matches BC1F/T condition tests and BC1FL/TL delay-slot annulment described by the manual.
findings.ctc1_reserved_bits: Unresolved: translator masks with 0x0183ffff; no CTC1 occurrence in measured corpus, and the manual text inspected does not specify reserved-bit write behavior.
findings.cfc1_fcr0: Bounded out-of-corpus field mismatch: pinned translator emits zero for FCR0, omitting documented implementation bits 15:8 = 0x2E. The revision byte is not specified numerically, so no full FCR0 value (including a claim of 0x2E00) is established. The saved inventory contains no CFC1.

limitations: No NaN behavior claim; Sony manual says the EE FPU does not support NaN.
PCSX2 is a software comparator, not a hardware oracle.
Counts are from saved function inventory instruction entries; there were no duplicate instruction addresses among these COP1 mnemonics.
No semantic equivalence claim for complete FPU behavior or generated game code.
The Sony User Manual specifies FCR0 implementation field 0x2E but not the specific silicon revision byte; this finding does not determine the entire runtime FCR0 value.
